92	/-- The atom ids a formula list reads, through atoms and primitives (a concept call is expanded first). -/
93	def formulaAtomIds (fs : List Formula) : List String :=
94	  ((fs.flatMap Formula.atoms).flatMap fun n =>
95	    if n.startsWith "prim_" then (Primitives.reads n).filterMap atomIdOf
96	    else (atomIdOf n).toList).flatMap kindDependencies |>.eraseDups
97	
98	/-- The atom ids a rule reads, through its atoms, its primitives and, transitively, the
99	    rules it composes. -/
100	def Rule.atomIds (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) : List String :=
101	  let rec go (fuel : Nat) (seen : List String) (r : Rule) : List String :=
102	    match fuel with
103	    | 0 => formulaAtomIds r.formulas
104	    | fuel + 1 =>
105	      formulaAtomIds r.formulas ++ (r.composes.flatMap fun id =>
106	        if seen.contains id then [] else
107	        match rules.find? (·.id == id) with
108	        | some r' => go fuel (id :: seen) r'
109	        | none => [])
110	  (go rules.length [r.id] r).eraseDups

112	inductive Support
113	  | supported
114	  | partially (absent : List String)      -- some atoms unobserved: verdicts may be unknown
115	  | unsupported (absent : List String)    -- the obligation reads nothing the source observes
116	  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited
117	
118	def Support.tag : Support → String
119	  | .supported => "supported"
120	  | .partially _ => "partial"
121	  | .unsupported _ => "unsupported"
122	def Support.absent : Support → List String
123	  | .supported => []
124	  | .partially a | .unsupported a => a
125	
126	/-- Support from syntax alone, closed over the rules a rule composes. Unsupported when every atom
127	    the obligation reads is absent (the rule could never decide), or a binder's class can never be
128	    established, or a composed rule is itself unsupported. -/
129	def support (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) (m : Manifest) : Support :=
130	  -- the clock is every source's: a window over time reads it, and no manifest declares it absent
131	  let absentOf (fs : List Formula) : List String × Nat :=
132	    let ids := (formulaAtomIds fs).filter (· != "kin.time")
133	    (ids.filter fun id => !m.observes id, ids.length)
134	  let (oblAbsent, oblTotal) := absentOf [r.obligation]
135	  let clsDead := r.binders.any fun b =>
136	    let (a, n) := absentOf [b.cls]
137	    n > 0 && a.length == n
138	  let composedDead := (r.composes.filterMap fun id => rules.find? (·.id == id)).any fun r' =>
139	    let (a, n) := absentOf [r'.obligation]
140	    n > 0 && a.length == n
141	  let allAbsent := (Rule.atomIds rules r).filter fun id => !m.observes id
142	  if allAbsent.isEmpty then .supported
143	  else if clsDead || composedDead || (oblTotal > 0 && oblAbsent.length == oblTotal) then .unsupported allAbsent
144	  else .partially allAbsent

    else

def rel_ahead_in_lane (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Bool := rel_ahead_behind_in_lane s a b
def rel_behind_in_lane (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Bool := rel_ahead_behind_in_lane s b a

/-- Signed overlap of the two footprints along `a`'s heading, each read with its own heading and
    extent: the length their projections on that axis share, positive when the bodies are side by
    side, otherwise the gap between the projections negated. A projection: it reads nothing across
    the axis, so a positive value is no contact and a negative one no distance between the bodies. -/
def rel_longitudinal_overlap (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Q :=
  match (s.relation a b).bind (·.longitudinalOverlap) with
  | some v => some v
  | none => do
    let pa ← kin_position s a
    let ha ← kin_heading s a
    let u ← Geom.unit ha
    let fa ← footprint s a
    let fb ← footprint s b
    let (loA, hiA) ← Geom.span u pa fa
    let (loB, hiB) ← Geom.span u pa fb
    pure (Q.sub (Q.min hiA hiB) (Q.max loA loB))

/-- Headings opposed (cosine below `-cosTol`) and the distance decreasing. -/
def rel_oncoming (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) (cosTol : Q) : Option Bool :=
  match (s.relation a b).bind (·.oncoming) with
  | some v => some v
  | none => do
    let ha ← kin_heading s a
    let hb ← kin_heading s b
    let pa ← kin_position s a
    let pb ← kin_position s b
    let va ← kin_velocity s a
    let vb ← kin_velocity s b
    let ua ← Geom.unit ha
    let ub ← Geom.unit hb
    let closing := Q.lt (Geom.dot (Geom.vsub pb pa) (Geom.vsub vb va)) Q.zero
    pure (Q.lt (Geom.dot ua ub) (Q.neg cosTol) && closing)

/-- Headings aligned (cosine above `cosTol`). -/
def rel_same_direction (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) (cosTol : Q) : Option Bool :=
  match (s.relation a b).bind (·.sameDirection) with
  | some v => some v
  | none => do
    let ha ← kin_heading s a
    let hb ← kin_heading s b
    let ua ← Geom.unit ha
    let ub ← Geom.unit hb
    pure (Q.gt (Geom.dot ua ub) cosTol)

/-- `b` relative to `a` in `a`'s frame: (longitudinal, lateral), lateral positive to the left. -/
def rel_bearing (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Vec :=
  match (s.relation a b).bind (·.bearing) with
  | some v => some v
  | none => relFrame s a b
def rel_bearing_right (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Bool := (rel_bearing s a b).map fun v => Q.lt v.2 Q.zero
def rel_bearing_left (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Bool := (rel_bearing s a b).map fun v => Q.gt v.2 Q.zero
def rel_bearing_ahead (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Bool := (rel_bearing s a b).map fun v => Q.gt v.1 Q.zero
def rel_bearing_behind (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Bool := (rel_bearing s a b).map fun v => Q.lt v.1 Q.zero

/-- The bodies touch or overlap. -/
def rel_contact (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Bool :=
  match (s.relation a b).bind (·.contact) with
  | some v => some v
  | none => (rel_surface_gap s a b).map fun g => Q.le g.1 Q.zero && Q.le g.2 Q.zero

/-
  Witnesses for NRS_484B_270_7b.

  Geometry (every figure is the witness's own and appears nowhere in the rule): a straight street
  along +x (east). Track 1 is the subject (a bicycle, half-extent 0.9 × 0.3 × 0.6 m; a moped of the
  same body in `idle`), track 2 the car passed (half-extent 2.25 × 0.9 × 0.75 m) on the line y = 0,
  heading east; track 3 an oncoming car (same body) heading west in `branch_2`. Instants k = 0 … 7
  at one-second spacing from t = 10 s; each trace is padded by repeating its first scene for 10 s
  before (car still well ahead) and its last scene for 2 s after, and `window` names the eight
  instants the witness speaks about.

  Bodies' projections on the subject's heading are disjoint when the centres are more than
  3.15 m apart along x. In the passes the car is ahead without overlap at k = 4 (4 m), alongside at
  k = 5, and behind without overlap at k = 6 (−4 m): the pass begins at k = 4 and is recognized at
  k = 6 (inside p.overtake_window = 10 s). Lateral offsets: y = 1.6 m gives a lateral gap between
  bodies of 0.4 m (below p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap = 1 m), y = 3 m one of 1.8 m (above it).
-/
import TrafficSpec.Rules.NRS_484B.NRS_484B_270_7b
import TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Builders

namespace TrafficSpecWitness.NRS_484B_270_7b

open TrafficSpec

def m (n : Int) : Q := Units.metres n
def cm (n : Int) : Q := Units.centimetres n

-- Binders ↦ tracks: subject ↦ 1

def bikeExt : Q × Q × Q := (cm 90, cm 30, cm 60)
def carExt : Q × Q × Q := (cm 225, cm 90, cm 75)

def t0 : Timestamp := 10000
def win : Option (Timestamp × Timestamp) := some (10000, 17000)

/-- The subject at (x, y) in centimetres, heading east. -/
def rider (cls : RoadUserClass) (x y : Int) (v : Int) : RoadUser :=
  Build.user 1 [cls] (cm x, cm y) Build.east (Units.metresPerSecond v) bikeExt

/-- The car passed, at x centimetres on y = 0, heading east. -/
def car (x : Int) (v : Int) : RoadUser :=
  Build.user 2 [.motorVehicle] (cm x, cm 0) Build.east (Units.metresPerSecond v) carExt

def ki (k : Nat) : Int := Int.ofNat k

/-- A pass of a car moving east at 2 m/s by a rider at 6 m/s on the line `y k` (cm). -/
def passTrace (cls : RoadUserClass) (y : Nat → Int) : Trace :=
  Build.pad
    (Build.trace 8 t0 (Units.seconds 1) fun k t =>
      Build.scene t (some 1)
        [ rider cls (600 * ki k) (y k) 6
        , car (2000 + 200 * ki k) 2 ]
        [ ] [ ])
    (Units.seconds 10) (Units.seconds 2) (Units.seconds 1)

/-- `forbid` (violated): A bicycle overtakes and passes a car moving slowly in the same direction, keeping a gap between bodies smaller than p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap while alongside. -/
def forbidTrace : Trace := passTrace .bicycle (fun _ => 160)

/-- `permit` (compliant): A bicycle overtakes and passes a slow car with a gap of at least p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap throughout the pass, no contact and no conflicting closest approach with any other road user. -/
def permitTrace : Trace := passTrace .bicycle (fun _ => 300)

/-- `idle` (not_applicable): The subject is a moped (outside the bicycle, electric bicycle and electric scooter aggregates, each of which leaves a moped out) overtaking and passing a car. -/
def idleTrace : Trace := passTrace .moped (fun _ => 160)

/-- `blind` (unknown): A bicycle overtakes and passes a car with no conflict with other road users; the gap between bodies is not observed on this source. -/
def blindTrace : Trace := passTrace .bicycle (fun _ => 300)

/-- `branch_3` (violated): A bicycle begins the pass of a car with a wide gap, then closes to a gap below p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap while still alongside before clearing the car: the pass is safe for part of the act only. -/
def branch_3Trace : Trace := passTrace .bicycle (fun k => if k ≤ 4 then 300 else 160)

/-- Branch 4: the rider's x (cm) per instant: close behind the car (0.5 m gap) at k = 0 … 2,
    then out to y = 3 m and past it. -/
def b4x (k : Nat) : Int :=
  match k with
  | 0 => 1635
  | 1 => 1835
  | 2 => 2035
  | 3 => 2100
  | 4 => 2600
  | 5 => 3100
  | 6 => 3600
  | _ => 4100

/-- `branch_4` (compliant): A bicycle follows close behind a car with a small gap before the pass begins, then moves out and keeps a gap of at least p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap at every observation from the pass's beginning to its recognition. -/
def branch_4Trace : Trace :=
  Build.pad
    (Build.trace 8 t0 (Units.seconds 1) fun k t =>
      Build.scene t (some 1)
        [ rider .bicycle (b4x k) (if k ≤ 2 then 0 else 300) 4
        , car (2000 + 200 * ki k) 2 ]
        [ ] [ ])
    (Units.seconds 10) (Units.seconds 2) (Units.seconds 1)

/-- `branch_1` (compliant): A bicycle rides on a street with no motor vehicle in the scene. -/
def branch_1Trace : Trace :=
  Build.pad
    (Build.trace 8 t0 (Units.seconds 1) fun k t =>
      Build.scene t (some 1)
        [ rider .bicycle (600 * ki k) 300 6 ]
        [ ] [ ])
    (Units.seconds 10) (Units.seconds 2) (Units.seconds 1)

/-- `branch_2` (violated): A bicycle overtakes and passes a standing car with a wide gap, but during the pass an oncoming car comes into a closest approach with the bicycle within p.conflict_horizon and below p.conflict_centre_clearance.
    The car stands at x = 20 m; the bicycle rides at 4 m/s on y = 3 m (1.8 m from the car's body);
    the oncoming car runs west at 10 m/s on y = 5.5 m, 2.5 m centre-to-centre laterally from the
    bicycle; at k = 4 they are 4 m apart along x and closing at 14 m/s. -/
def branch_2Trace : Trace :=
  Build.pad
    (Build.trace 8 t0 (Units.seconds 1) fun k t =>
      Build.scene t (some 1)
        [ rider .bicycle (400 * ki k) 300 4
        , car 2000 0
        , Build.user 3 [.motorVehicle] (cm (6000 - 1000 * ki k), cm 550) Build.west
            (Units.metresPerSecond 10) carExt ]
        [ ] [ ])
    (Units.seconds 10) (Units.seconds 2) (Units.seconds 1)

def witness (name : String) (τ : Trace) (expected : Verdict)
    (absent : List String := []) (boundary : String := "") : Scenario :=
  { name := name
    rule := "NRS_484B_270_7b"
    trace := τ
    reading := {}          -- ignored by the gate: the run's reading is substituted
    manifest := Build.manifest absent
    grounding := [("subject", 1)]
    expected := expected
    window := win
    boundary := boundary }

def scenarios : List Scenario :=
  [ witness "forbid" forbidTrace .violated
  , witness "permit" permitTrace .compliant
  , witness "idle" idleTrace .notApplicable
  , witness "blind" blindTrace (.unknown []) ["rel.surface_gap"]
  , witness "branch_3" branch_3Trace .violated
  , witness "branch_4" branch_4Trace .compliant
  , witness "branch_1" branch_1Trace .compliant
  , witness "branch_2" branch_2Trace .violated ]

end TrafficSpecWitness.NRS_484B_270_7b

/-

  along +x (east). Track 1 is the subject (a bicycle, half-extent 0.9 × 0.3 × 0.6 m; a moped of the

  heading east; track 3 an oncoming car (same body) heading west in `branch_2`. Instants k = 0 … 7
  at one-second spacing from t = 10 s; each trace is padded by repeating its first scene for 10 s
  before (car still well ahead) and its last scene for 2 s after, and `window` names the eight
  instants the witness speaks about.

  Bodies' projections on the subject's heading are disjoint when the centres are more than
  3.15 m apart along x. In the passes the car is ahead without overlap at k = 4 (4 m), alongside at
  k = 5, and behind without overlap at k = 6 (−4 m): the pass begins at k = 4 and is recognized at
  k = 6 (inside p.overtake_window = 10 s). Lateral offsets: y = 1.6 m gives a lateral gap between
  bodies of 0.4 m (below p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap = 1 m), y = 3 m one of 1.8 m (above it).

import TrafficSpec.Rules.NRS_484B.NRS_484B_270_7b
import TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Builders

namespace TrafficSpecWitness.NRS_484B_270_7b

open TrafficSpec

def m (n : Int) : Q := Units.metres n
def cm (n : Int) : Q := Units.centimetres n

-- Binders ↦ tracks: subject ↦ 1

def bikeExt : Q × Q × Q := (cm 90, cm 30, cm 60)
def carExt : Q × Q × Q := (cm 225, cm 90, cm 75)

def t0 : Timestamp := 10000
def win : Option (Timestamp × Timestamp) := some (10000, 17000)

/-- The subject at (x, y) in centimetres, heading east. -/
def rider (cls : RoadUserClass) (x y : Int) (v : Int) : RoadUser :=
  Build.user 1 [cls] (cm x, cm y) Build.east (Units.metresPerSecond v) bikeExt

/-- The car passed, at x centimetres on y = 0, heading east. -/
def car (x : Int) (v : Int) : RoadUser :=
  Build.user 2 [.motorVehicle] (cm x, cm 0) Build.east (Units.metresPerSecond v) carExt

def ki (k : Nat) : Int := Int.ofNat k

/-- A pass of a car moving east at 2 m/s by a rider at 6 m/s on the line `y k` (cm). -/
def passTrace (cls : RoadUserClass) (y : Nat → Int) : Trace :=
  Build.pad
    (Build.trace 8 t0 (Units.seconds 1) fun k t =>
      Build.scene t (some 1)
        [ rider cls (600 * ki k) (y k) 6
        , car (2000 + 200 * ki k) 2 ]
        [ ] [ ])
    (Units.seconds 10) (Units.seconds 2) (Units.seconds 1)

/-- `forbid` (violated): A bicycle overtakes and passes a car moving slowly in the same direction, keeping a gap between bodies smaller than p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap while alongside. -/
def forbidTrace : Trace := passTrace .bicycle (fun _ => 160)

/-- `permit` (compliant): A bicycle overtakes and passes a slow car with a gap of at least p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap throughout the pass, no contact and no conflicting closest approach with any other road user. -/
def permitTrace : Trace := passTrace .bicycle (fun _ => 300)

/-- `idle` (not_applicable): The subject is a moped (outside the bicycle, electric bicycle and electric scooter aggregates, each of which leaves a moped out) overtaking and passing a car. -/
def idleTrace : Trace := passTrace .moped (fun _ => 160)

/-- No body extent observed: the source gives positions and headings, and measures the
    longitudinal overlap, the contact and the gap between the bodies itself (the gap is dropped
    by the manifest). -/
def noExtent (u : RoadUser) : RoadUser := Build.withKin u fun k => { k with extent := none }

/-- The overlap of the bodies' projections (cm) in the pass geometry: 3.15 m less the distance
    between the centres along x. -/
def blindOverlap (k : Nat) : Int :=
  let d := 2000 - 400 * ki k
  315 - (if d < 0 then -d else d)

/-- `blind` (unknown): A bicycle overtakes and passes a car with no conflict with other road users; the gap between bodies is not observed on this source.
    The permit geometry (y = 3 m, lateral gap 1.8 m), with the extents unobserved and the overlap,
    contact and gap supplied as measured relations from the bicycle to the car. -/
def blindTrace : Trace :=
  Build.pad
    (Build.trace 8 t0 (Units.seconds 1) fun k t =>
      Build.withRelations
        (Build.scene t (some 1)
          [ noExtent (rider .bicycle (600 * ki k) 300 6)
          , noExtent (car (2000 + 200 * ki k) 2) ]
          [ ] [ ])
        [ Build.relation 1 2 fun r =>
            { r with longitudinalOverlap := some (cm (blindOverlap k))
                     contact := some false
                     surfaceGap := some (cm 0, cm 180) } ])
    (Units.seconds 10) (Units.seconds 2) (Units.seconds 1)

/-- `branch_3` (violated): A bicycle begins the pass of a car with a wide gap, then closes to a gap below p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap while still alongside before clearing the car: the pass is safe for part of the act only. -/
def branch_3Trace : Trace := passTrace .bicycle (fun k => if k ≤ 4 then 300 else 160)

/-- Branch 4: the rider's x (cm) per instant: close behind the car (0.5 m gap) at k = 0 … 2,
    then out to y = 3 m and past it. -/
def b4x (k : Nat) : Int :=
  match k with
  | 0 => 1635
  | 1 => 1835
  | 2 => 2035
  | 3 => 2100
  | 4 => 2600
  | 5 => 3100
  | 6 => 3600
  | _ => 4100

/-- `branch_4` (compliant): A bicycle follows close behind a car with a small gap before the pass begins, then moves out and keeps a gap of at least p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap at every observation from the pass's beginning to its recognition. -/
def branch_4Trace : Trace :=
  Build.pad
    (Build.trace 8 t0 (Units.seconds 1) fun k t =>
      Build.scene t (some 1)
        [ rider .bicycle (b4x k) (if k ≤ 2 then 0 else 300) 4
        , car (2000 + 200 * ki k) 2 ]
        [ ] [ ])
    (Units.seconds 10) (Units.seconds 2) (Units.seconds 1)

/-- `branch_1` (compliant): A bicycle rides on a street with no motor vehicle in the scene. -/
def branch_1Trace : Trace :=
  Build.pad
    (Build.trace 8 t0 (Units.seconds 1) fun k t =>
      Build.scene t (some 1)
        [ rider .bicycle (600 * ki k) 300 6 ]
        [ ] [ ])
    (Units.seconds 10) (Units.seconds 2) (Units.seconds 1)

/-- `branch_2` (violated): A bicycle overtakes and passes a standing car with a wide gap, but during the pass an oncoming car comes into a closest approach with the bicycle within p.conflict_horizon and below p.conflict_centre_clearance.
    The car stands at x = 20 m; the bicycle rides at 4 m/s on y = 3 m (1.8 m from the car's body);
    the oncoming car runs west at 10 m/s on y = 5.5 m, 2.5 m centre-to-centre laterally from the
    bicycle; at k = 4 they are 4 m apart along x and closing at 14 m/s. -/
def branch_2Trace : Trace :=
  Build.pad
    (Build.trace 8 t0 (Units.seconds 1) fun k t =>
      Build.scene t (some 1)
        [ rider .bicycle (400 * ki k) 300 4
        , car 2000 0
        , Build.user 3 [.motorVehicle] (cm (6000 - 1000 * ki k), cm 550) Build.west
            (Units.metresPerSecond 10) carExt ]
        [ ] [ ])
    (Units.seconds 10) (Units.seconds 2) (Units.seconds 1)

def witness (name : String) (τ : Trace) (expected : Verdict)
    (absent : List String := []) (boundary : String := "") : Scenario :=
  { name := name
    rule := "NRS_484B_270_7b"
    trace := τ
    reading := {}          -- ignored by the gate: the run's reading is substituted
    manifest := Build.manifest absent
    grounding := [("subject", 1)]
    expected := expected
    window := win
    boundary := boundary }

def scenarios : List Scenario :=
  [ witness "forbid" forbidTrace .violated
  , witness "permit" permitTrace .compliant
  , witness "idle" idleTrace .notApplicable
  , witness "blind" blindTrace (.unknown []) ["rel.surface_gap"]
  , witness "branch_3" branch_3Trace .violated
  , witness "branch_4" branch_4Trace .compliant
  , witness "branch_1" branch_1Trace .compliant
  , witness "branch_2" branch_2Trace .violated ]

end TrafficSpecWitness.NRS_484B_270_7b

# NRS_484B_270_7b — task result

**Final verdict: OK** (8 witnesses, 10 names, composes nothing)

## Gate runs

1. `UNUSED_CLAIM` — run by mistake on the harness skeleton before any edit (every claim unused).
   Changed nothing on that basis.
2. `WITNESS_FAIL` — blind: expected unknown, got compliant. Cause: masking `rel.surface_gap`
   only drops a *measured* gap. Core still computed the gap from the bodies' footprints
   (position, heading, extent).
3. A gate invocation I issued by mistake as a background job with a 1 ms timeout. It was killed
   before it reported anything. It may still have counted against the budget.
4. `WITNESS_FAIL` (same as run 2) — another accidental invocation, on unchanged files.
5. `WITNESS_FAIL` — I rebuilt blind without body extents and supplied overlap, contact and gap.
   The admission check rejected the trace on two counts:
   - the tracks were in `occupancyObserved` without a footprint;
   - with a gap supplied, Core computes `rel.contact` from it, so contact must not be supplied.
   Fix: set `occupancyObserved := []` (the rule reads no occupancy) and stopped supplying the
   gap. Only `longitudinalOverlap` and `contact` are now supplied, and Core cannot compute
   either on that scene.
6. `OK`.

Runs 1, 3 and 4 were my errors in issuing commands, not gate behaviour.

## How the rule is written

The gate returns **OK** for NRS_484B_270_7b: all 8 witnesses reach their planned verdicts.

**The rule.** The subject must be a bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter (the three admitted aggregates). The duty applies to every other road user `m` that is a motor vehicle. At the moment the pass is recognized (`drv_interaction_overtake_pass`), the pass must have been safe from its beginning up to that moment:

`since (safe ∧ ¬aheadAligned) (aheadAligned ∧ safe)`

- **`aheadAligned`** is the beginning as the concept's contract defines it: `m` is ahead along the subject's heading, the bodies don't overlap lengthwise, and the headings are aligned.
- **`safe`** means three things: no contact with `m`, a gap of at least `p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap` between the bodies, and no other road user in a near-collision approach within `p.conflict_horizon` and below `p.conflict_centre_clearance`.
- **Why `¬aheadAligned` is in the left operand:** it makes the search stop at the pass's beginning, so nothing earlier is read. On decided values this gives the same verdicts as the plainer `since safe (aheadAligned ∧ safe)`. It is a way of writing the record, not a narrowing of it, so no narrowing is declared. Applicability is `.tt`, since the node has no trigger or condition span.

**The blind witness took the most work.** Hiding the gap only drops a gap the source supplies; Core still computes it from the bodies' sizes. So I built that witness without body sizes and supplied the lengthwise overlap and contact as measured values, which Core can't compute on that scene. The admission check then required two more changes: no occupancy observation for those tracks (the rule reads none), and no supplied gap at all.

**Gate budget:** I used it carelessly. Of 6 runs, at least 5 were spent:
- one on the untouched skeleton;
- two by mistake, one on unchanged files and one killed before it reported (that one may not have counted);
- two that showed the blind problem;
- the final OK.

I also issued two other shell commands by mistake; both were denied and nothing ran.

`task_result.md` in the working directory has the run log and the choices made.
